name: Grand Canyon National Park
blurb: Rim forests, desert slopes, and the scavengers that ride the canyon air.

tip.title: Take away fire
tip.text: Frequent low fires keep ponderosa forest open and its grasses growing. Set Low-intensity fire to -100% and watch the pines and grasses, then the elk, deer and bighorn that graze there.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Grand Canyon National Park, Kaibab squirrel, California condor). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives plant growth on the rims and canyon slopes, though water is usually the limit.
Rain and snow vary a lot with elevation: the North Rim gets far more precipitation and snow than the South Rim, and water limits plant life across the canyon.

nodes.name: Fungi & soil microbes
nodes.desc: Break down dead wood, needles, grasses and carcasses and return nutrients to thin canyon-country soils.

nodes.name: Ponderosa pine
nodes.desc: Dominant tree of the cooler rim forests. Its seeds feed squirrels and chipmunks, and its seedlings are browsed by mule deer.
A small pine of the drier woodland below the pine forest. Rock squirrels are recorded eating its seeds.
A shrubby oak whose acorns and leaves feed squirrels, mice and browsing deer on the rims.
A tough desert shrub that deer browse on dry slopes.

nodes.name: Grasses
nodes.desc: Bunchgrasses and other grasses grow in open forest and on dry ground and feed elk, deer and bighorn.
A large grazer of rim meadows and open forest. Cougars and coyotes take elk, and their carcasses feed scavengers.
Browses shrubs and young pines on the rims and is a main prey of cougars and a main carcass for scavengers.
A climber of canyon cliffs that grazes and browses. Cougars take bighorn sheep, among other large prey.
A common ground squirrel of rocky slopes. GloBI records it eating juniper and pinyon seeds, and hawks and coyotes prey on it.
Lives in ponderosa pine forest and eats pine seeds. Its Kaibab race lives only on the Kaibab Plateau, including the North Rim.
A small, widespread omnivore that eats seeds and insects and is food for hawks and coyotes.
Hunts small mammals and also eats carrion. GloBI records it eating rock squirrels, mice and deer.
A soaring hawk that hunts squirrels and mice from the rim and canyon updrafts.
A clever scavenger and the most recorded bird near the park. It feeds on carrion and scraps.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds carcasses by smell and feeds on carrion. GloBI records it eating mule deer and rock squirrels.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: Deer and elk are its main prey, and it also takes bighorn sheep. It lives in forests and rugged canyon country.

story: Grand Canyon National Park covers 1,901 square miles of northwestern Arizona around a gorge of the Colorado River. UNESCO named it a World Heritage Site in 1979. The Kaibab squirrel lives only in the ponderosa forests of the North Rim, eating pine seeds and underground truffles.
matters: The Kaibab squirrel, the ponderosa pines and the fungi near them depend on one another. The squirrel lives only on the Kaibab Plateau.
